_comment: Copy this to data/macros.json to give one name to several commands.
Your file is merged over the built-in macros in skills/macros.py.
A step is just something you would SAY. There is no separate macro
language to learn -- each step goes back through the brain exactly as
if you had spoken it, so anything Jarvis can do, a macro can do.
steps   the commands, in order. Required.
say     what to say when it finishes. Leave it out and Jarvis reads
you the answers instead -- which is what you want for a
macro made of questions.
pause   seconds between steps (default 0.6). Raise it if an app is
slow to take focus and the next step lands in the wrong
window.
To run one, say its name on its own: 'start work'. A name on its own
beats every other rule, which is why 'start work' opens your three
apps rather than looking for an app called 'work'. Anything MORE than
the bare name goes to the normal rules, so naming a macro 'notes'
does not stop 'read me my notes' from working.
You never have to edit this file. Say instead:
create a macro called start work: open chrome, open spotify
list my macros
what does the start work macro do
forget the start work macro
Setting a name to null deletes a built-in -- see 'wind down' below.
Restart Jarvis after editing by hand.
